B.domain: Subtraction of fractions and mixed numbers with simplification to lowest terms

skills.name: Normalize operands
skills.definition: Rewrite a quantity into a subtraction-ready equivalent form, such as simplifying a fraction part, converting an improper mixed number to a standard mixed number, or expressing a whole number as a mixed number with fractional part 0.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step rewrites a mixed number with an improper fraction part into an equivalent standard mixed number.
Tag when a step simplifies a fractional part before subtraction, such as 4/10 to 2/5.
Tag when a step rewrites a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a denominator to align mixed-number subtraction.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when the step only finds a common denominator for unlike fractions without changing number type.
Do not tag when the step only performs subtraction after the numbers are already in usable form.
Do not tag final combining or simplification of the result unless the step is explicitly rewriting an operand before subtraction.

skills.name: Common denominator conversion
skills.definition: Find a common denominator and convert fractional parts to equivalent fractions with that denominator before subtracting.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step finds an LCD or common denominator for unlike denominators.
Tag when a step converts one or both fractions to equivalent fractions with the common denominator.
Tag even if the denominators are already equal but the solution explicitly performs the denominator-alignment step.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when fractions already share a denominator and no conversion is performed.
Do not tag rewriting a whole number as 0 over a denominator; that belongs to operand normalization.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping from the whole part.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Subtract fractions with aligned denominators and/or subtract the whole and fractional parts of mixed numbers before any needed regrouping.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step subtracts numerators of fractions that already have the same denominator.
Tag when a step subtracts whole parts and fraction parts separately in a mixed-number problem.
Tag when the subtraction produces zero or a negative fractional part prior to borrowing.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag steps whose main purpose is finding a common denominator or converting forms before subtraction.
Do not tag borrowing/regrouping steps that adjust the whole and fractional parts after an initial negative fraction result.
Do not tag final simplification or combining unless actual subtraction is performed in that step.

skills.name: Regroup and simplify result
skills.definition: Regroup by borrowing 1 from the whole part when the fractional subtraction is negative, and simplify or express the final result in lowest terms, integer form, or mixed-number form.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a step borrows 1 from the whole part and converts it into denominator-over-denominator to continue subtraction.
Tag when a step simplifies a resulting fraction such as 9/12 to 3/4 or 0/3 to 0.
Tag when a step combines the final whole and fractional parts into the reported answer.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag initial rewriting of operands before subtraction; that belongs to operand normalization.
Do not tag common-denominator conversion before subtraction.
Do not tag straightforward subtraction steps that do not involve regrouping or final-result simplification/assembly.

A.domain: Subtraction of fractions and mixed numbers with simplification

skills.name: Normalize operands
skills.definition: Rewrite a whole number or nonstandard mixed number into a subtraction-ready form, such as adding a 0-fraction part or converting an improper fractional part to a standard mixed number.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution rewrites a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a denominator, such as 3 = 3 + 0/5.
Tag when a solution converts a mixed number with an improper fraction part into an equivalent standard mixed number, such as 2 3/2 = 3 1/2.
Tag when a solution simplifies a fractional part inside a mixed number before subtraction, such as 3 4/10 = 3 2/5.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when the operands are already in usable form and no rewriting is performed.
Do not tag denominator-matching steps whose purpose is to create equivalent fractions for subtraction; those belong to common-denominator work.
Do not tag final simplification of the answer after subtraction.

skills.name: Match denominators
skills.definition: Find a common denominator and convert fraction parts to equivalent fractions with that denominator before subtracting.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution explicitly finds an LCD or common denominator.
Tag when a solution converts one or both fractions to equivalent fractions with the same denominator.
Tag for mixed-number problems when only the fractional parts are adjusted to a common denominator.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when fractions already share a denominator and no conversion is needed.
Do not tag rewriting a whole number as a mixed number with 0 over a denominator; that is operand normalization.
Do not tag borrowing from the whole part to the fractional part.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Subtract fractions with like denominators and/or subtract the whole-number and fractional parts of mixed numbers once the forms are aligned.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution subtracts numerators of like-denominator fractions.
Tag when a solution subtracts whole parts and fraction parts separately in a mixed-number problem.
Tag when a solution recomputes the fractional subtraction after denominator matching or after borrowing.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag steps whose main purpose is to create equivalent fractions with a common denominator.
Do not tag the borrowing action itself when the fractional part would otherwise be negative.
Do not tag simplification-only steps such as reducing 9/12 to 3/4 or 0/3 to 0.

skills.name: Borrow and simplify
skills.definition: Regroup one whole into fractional units when needed and express the final result in lowest terms or integer form.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution borrows 1 from the whole part and converts it into denominator-sized fractional units, such as 1 = 5/5 or 1 = 24/24.
Tag when a solution reduces a fraction to lowest terms after subtraction.
Tag when a solution simplifies a zero fraction to 0 or combines a zero whole part with a fraction into a simpler final form.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag ordinary subtraction steps that do not involve regrouping.
Do not tag initial rewriting of operands before subtraction; that is operand normalization.
Do not tag common-denominator conversion steps.

C.domain: Subtraction of fractions and mixed numbers, including common denominators, unlike denominators, regrouping, normalization, and simplification

skills.name: Normalize number forms
skills.definition: Rewrite a whole number or mixed number into a subtraction-ready equivalent form, such as adding a zero fractional part or converting a mixed number with an improper fractional part to a standard mixed number.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution rewrites a whole number as a whole plus 0/n before subtracting.
Tag when a solution converts a mixed number with an improper fraction part into an equivalent standard mixed number.
Tag when a solution simplifies or normalizes a fractional part inside a mixed number before subtraction so the mixed number is in a more usable equivalent form.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when the step only finds a common denominator for two fractions already being subtracted.
Do not tag when the step only performs subtraction after the numbers are already in usable form.
Do not tag when the step only simplifies the final answer after subtraction.

skills.name: Create common denominator
skills.definition: Find a least common denominator and convert fractional parts to equivalent fractions with that denominator before subtraction.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution explicitly finds an LCD or common denominator for unlike denominators.
Tag when a solution converts one or both fractions to equivalent fractions with the same denominator.
Tag when mixed-number fraction parts are rewritten to a common denominator before subtracting.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when denominators are already the same and no conversion is needed.
Do not tag when a step only rewrites a whole number as 0/n.
Do not tag when a step only simplifies a result such as 9/12 to 3/4.

skills.name: Subtract aligned parts
skills.definition: Subtract fractions with a common denominator and/or subtract the whole and fractional parts of mixed numbers once the parts are aligned.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution subtracts numerators over a shared denominator.
Tag when a solution subtracts whole parts and fraction parts of mixed numbers without needing regrouping in that step.
Tag when a solution combines the computed whole and fractional differences into a mixed number or integer result.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when the main work is finding a common denominator or converting forms before subtraction.
Do not tag when the key step is borrowing or regrouping because the fractional subtraction would otherwise be negative.
Do not tag when the step only reduces a fraction to lowest terms after subtraction.

skills.name: Regroup and simplify
skills.definition: Borrow one whole to continue subtraction when the fractional part is too small, and reduce any resulting fraction or zero form to lowest terms.
inclusion_criteria: Tag when a solution borrows 1 from the whole part and converts it into denominator/denominator for the fractional subtraction.
Tag when a solution resolves a negative fractional difference by regrouping across the whole and fraction parts.
Tag when a solution simplifies a non-final or final fraction result, including reducing to an integer such as 0/3 = 0 or 9/12 = 3/4.
exclusion_criteria: Do not tag when subtraction is completed directly without borrowing or simplification.
Do not tag when the step only finds an LCD or rewrites numbers into equivalent starting forms.
Do not tag when a step merely states the final combined answer without regrouping or simplification work.
